title: CPSC, KitchenAid Announce Recall to Repair Food Processors
summary: A cap on the blade unit can dislodge during use. When dislodged, the cap can get mixed in with food, presenting a choking hazard. Units: About 220,000.

title: CPSC, Playworld Systems Announce Recall of Playground Swings
summary: The swings connectors, which attach the top bar to the end supports, can crack and the top bar can break off and hit children on the swings. Units: About 370.

title: CPSC, Zebco Announce Recall of Compact Camper Stoves
summary: These camper stoves could have been shipped with butane already in the fuel compartment, posing a fire and burn hazard. Also, because of a possible problem with the fuel control mechanism, the stoves could flare up or catch fire when operated. Units: About 9,600.

title: CPSC, Pottery Barn Kids Inc. Announce Recall of Bunk Beds
summary: The side rail and guardrails on these beds can break, causing the bed to collapse and allowing childen to fall out of the beds. Units: About 200.

title: CPSC, Power Tool Manufacturers Announce Recall of Various Power Tools
summary: The switches on these power tools, which were manufactured by Eaton Corp, of Cleveland, Ohio, can stick. The tools can continue to operate after the trigger has been released, posing a risk of injury to consumers. Units: About 180,000.

title: CPSC, Dell Announce Recall of Batteries for Notebook-Computers
summary: These batteries can short circuit, even when the battery is not in use, causing them to become very hot, release smoke and possibly catch fire. Units: About 27,000.

title: CPSC, NHTSA and Century Announce Recall of Infant Car Seats/Carriers
summary: When the seat is used as an infant carrier, the handle can break. An infant inside the carrier can fall to the ground and suffer serious injuries. title: CPSC, DeWALT® Industrial Tool Co. Announce Recall of Battery Chargers
summary: Metal clips inside the chargers could come loose and stick through the chargers' vents, possibly resulting in consumers receiving an electrical shock. Units: About 825,000.

title: CPSC, RockShox Inc. Announce Recall of Bicycle Forks
summary: The compression rods inside these forks can break, causing the rider to lose control of the bicycle, fall, and possibly suffer serious injuries. Units: About 220,000.

title: CPSC, I-Tech Sport Products Inc. Announce Recall to Replace Hockey Face Guards
summary: These face guards, which attach to helmets, can become dislodged on impact, causing them to fall off, leaving the user's face exposed to possible injury. Units: About 1,000.

title: CPSC, Woods Industries Announce Recall of Extension Cords and Cord Reels
summary: The extension cords and cord reels are equipped with a locking plug, which is designed to keep tools plugged in. The plastic housing of the locking plug can separate or break, exposing consumers to live wires and posing shock and electrocution hazards. Units: About 500,000.

title: CPSC, The Sharper Image Recall Motorized CD Racks
summary: Batteries in the unit can leak or explode, when used with an AC adapter. Consumers can suffer burns from the leaking battery or can be struck by pieces of an exploding battery. Units: About 1,000.

title: CPSC, Compaq Announce Recall of Notebook Computer Battery Packs
summary: These battery packs can short circuit, causing them to overheat, release smoke and possibly catch fire. Units: About 55,000.

title: CPSC, The Betesh Group Announce Recall of "John Lennon" Crib Mobiles
summary: The screws that connect the mobile's arm assembly and crib clamp can become loose if overtightened. The arms can detach and fall into the crib, injuring the baby inside. Units: About 47,000.

title: CPSC, Playworld Systems Announce Recall of Playground Slides
summary: The welding of the slide bed to the slide sidewall can crack and separate and children's fingers can get caught in the space, posing a risk of amputation. Units: 55.

title: CPSC, Toro Co. Announce Recall of Lawn Mowers
summary: The wiring on these mowers can short circuit, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 23,000.

title: CPSC, Appliance Manufacturers Announce Voluntary Recall Initiative for Old Chest Freezers - A Deadly Play Area for Children
summary: Although some manufacturers had freezers that were in compliance prior to the 1970 standards, most old chest freezers have latches that can trap a child.
